name: Gastric and Duodenal Anatomy and Peptic Perforation

reference.source: ALGrawany Anatomy & Physiology Made Easy 2026 / Sabiston Surgery 22e
clinicalPearls: Stomach blood supply derives from celiac trunk via gastric, gastroepiploic, and short gastric vessels
Posterior duodenal bulb (D1) ulcers erode gastroduodenal artery, causing life-threatening hematemesis
Anterior duodenal bulb ulcers perforate into peritoneal cavity, causing peritonitis and pneumoperitoneum
Ampulla of Vater empties into second part of duodenum (D2), guarded by sphincter of Oddi
Third part of duodenum (D3) crosses horizontally between aorta and superior mesenteric artery (SMA syndrome)
reference.pathophysiology: The gastroduodenal mucosa balances mucosal defense factors (mucus, bicarbonate, mucosal blood flow) against aggressive luminal forces (gastric hydrochloric acid, pepsin, Helicobacter pylori). Ulcer penetration through the muscularis mucosae can erode into submucosal arterial branches or perforate the free anterior visceral wall.
additionalDifferentials: Bleeding peptic ulcer with gastroduodenal artery erosion
additionalInvestigations: Erect chest radiograph to detect free air under diaphragm (pneumoperitoneum)
Contrast-enhanced CT abdomen for perforated peptic ulcer and fluid collections
